"SSW will acquire Delivery Hero's businesses in a total of 14 markets, particularly where Uber Eats and Delivery Hero already overlap," the statement said, in a deal worth approximately $1.6 billion. https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026.text: The average number of people travelling on each Channel-crossing dinghy has sharply increased in recent years. Photograph: SNMS Berck sur Mer/AFP/Getty Images View image in fullscreen The average number of people travelling on each Channel-crossing dinghy has sharply increased in recent years. Photograph: SNMS Berck sur Mer/AFP/Getty Images Immigration and asylum How to buy a ‘mega-dinghy’: the perilous new model of Channel crossing Boats carrying hundreds of people are a clear and alarming trend. But where do such large vessels come from? Daniel Boffey Chief reporter Sat 15 Aug 2026 08.00 EDT Last modified on Sat 15 Aug 2026 08.15 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google P roviding a large dinghy for use in the choppy seas of western Europe was not a problem, as long as the order was for more than 20 vessels, they said. The sales manager at the Chinese company even had an online brochure for an undercover Guardian reporter, posing as a prospective client, to peruse. They had a production capacity of 500 boats a month and, yes, it was possible to get even bigger ones for the right price. They could do a seven or even an eight-metre military-style dinghy for $1,678 (£1,238) a boat, without the engines, but that would be lacking CE certification, the mandatory mark that shows a product meets EU health and safety requirements. “We can sell this big boat to China warehouse only,” wrote the sales manager on the Made in China messaging platform. From there, it was up to the client to export it and get the right certification. In the early hours of Monday morning, a full-to-the-brim dinghy of a type similar to that being offered by the Chinese salesperson arrived in the UK after crossing the Channel with a record 230 people onboard . French authorities say there have been 11 such “mega-dinghy” crossings of the Channel so far this year. Last week one of those carrying 173 people capsized after its engine caught fire. It is a clear and perilous trend. An analysis by the Migration Observatory at the University of Oxford, based on Home Office figures, shows how the number of people travelling on a dinghy has sharply increased since the crossings first began nearly a decade ago. In 2018, there would be an average of seven people per small boat. That ticked up to 13 by 2020. The number shifted up to 27 by the following year and by 2022 it was 41. The average number of people on a dinghy crossing is up to 66.5 people in the first six months of 2026. These are often no longer small boats. The length of the dinghy that arrived this week was 15 metres. Graph: average number of people per dinghy each year since 2018 Where are the “mega-dinghies” coming from? The sales manager offering boats to an undercover Guardian reporter worked for a company called Wuxi Funsor Marine Equipment that is described on its own website as a subsidiary of the Weihai Yamar Outdoors Product Co Ltd. Weihai Yamar, which is headquartered in an industrial park in Wenquan Town in Weihai, in the eastern Chinese province of Shandong, was put under economic sanctions by the UK in July last year for offering rigid inflatable boats for sale on online retail platforms to organised crime gangs smuggling people across the Channel. Weihai’s largest shareholder at the time is now the main shareholder of Wuxi Funsor Marine Equipment. Weihai Yamar has denied advertising lifeboats and boats for migrants online. The likely onward journey of dinghies from eastern China can be traced thanks to the recent trial of Adem Savas, a Turkish national identified by the National Crime Agency (NCA) as one of the key enablers of small boat crossings . Between 2019 and 2024, Savas was said by the NCA to have supplied inflatable boats, outboard engines and equipment to gangs across Europe, enabling thousands of crossings, including around half of all Channel crossings in 2023, generating millions of pounds in profit. Savas was the primary equipment supplier to a Kurdish smuggler, Hewa Rahimpur . The boats and engines were sourced largely from China, transported from Turkey through Bulgaria, and stored in Germany before onward distribution to smuggling networks in Belgium and France. A Netherlands-based haulage firm facilitated the logistics. A raid coordinated by Europol in December 2024 resulted in 25 searches in Germany and the seizure of equipment and cash. Savas pleaded guilty in a court in Bruges to people-smuggling and being a member of an organised crime group and was sentenced to 11 years’ imprisonment and a €400,000 (£340,000) fine. Savas’s co-defendants received combined sentences of 38 years. A spokesperson for Europol said the shift to larger boats was plausibly an indication that the gangs were getting desperate. “I can confirm that Europol – and within our agency specifically the experts forming the European Centre Against Migrant Smuggling (ECAMS) – is aware of this development,” the spokesperson said. “We are in constant exchange with the appropriate authorities in both France and the United Kingdom on this phenomenon and also have a dedicated operational taskforce running that concentrates on smuggling of migrants with boats (no matter if relatively small boats or, as of recently, larger boats) across the Channel. “As with any criminal phenomenon, a change of tactics used by criminal networks may be the result of law enforcement pressure.” Mihnea Cuibus, a senior researcher at the Migration Observatory, said the mega-dinghy phenomenon made economic sense for the gangs as they faced pressures on their supply chains from the authorities. “It’s simply much more efficient, much more profitable for gangs to pack as many people as possible on one boat,” he said. “What we’ve seen in the last few weeks with some of these so-called mega-dinghies is an acceleration of this longstanding trend. “It’s very likely to do with increased enforcement in and around the French coast in particular. We’ve seen the authorities work, quite differently, targeting the supply chains and making it hard to get hold of the small boats in the first place.” Weihai Yamar did not respond to a request for comment. Beállítom „Kemény, nehéz időkben, olyan bátor, tökös emberekre volt szükség, mint Magyar Péter, vagy Én. Majd egyenesbe jön az ország és jöhetnek a gyengék, a puhák” – üzente egy Facebook-posztban egy őt üzenetben szidó szavazónak Ferenczi Gábor, a Tisza hódmezővásárhelyi országgyűlési képviselője. Részletesen leírta, tiszta szívvel vállalja, hogy megszavazta Unger Annát a vagyonvisszaszerzési hivatal elnökének. Érzelmesre sikerült posztja elején Ferenczi megkérdezte: „Az rendben van, hogy a messengeremre tegnap este 23 óra után jön egy mocskolódó üzenet, hogy én hogy képzeltem, hogy Unger Annát megszavaztam és nem Ligetit?” Majd úgy folytatta, hogy „pedig Ő még a szökőkúthoz is kijött a kampányban, hogy meghallgassa a beszédem! Te hős!” Ferenczi Gábor miután megköszönte, hogy az illető „kijött a szökőkúthoz a rendszerváltásért, sőt szavazott is” részletezi, hogy milyen áldozatokat hozott a képviselőségért: bezárta a vállalkozását, hat hónapon át egy fillért sem keresett, napi pár órákat aludva felszántotta a választókerületet, „miközbe egy suttyó alak hazugságot terjesztve akart lejáratni a promenád és a makói televízió hathatós közreműködése közepette”. Ferenczi szerint mindezt a rendszerváltásért, az elszámoltatásért, az igazságért és a hazáért tette. Majd az kérdezte, hogy „azért dögöljön meg”, mert bízik a szakmailag felkészült (jogász, ügyész, ügyvéd stb.) képviselőtársaiban, akik az Igazságügyi Bizottság tagjaként kiválasztották a szerintük legalkalmasabb embert a hivatal vezetésére. „Igen, nem fogok laikusok facebook kommentjei, meg feltűnési viszketegségben szenvedő emberek posztjai alapján szavazni arról, hogy Unger Anna megkapja a bizalmat vagy sem!” – írta. A képviselő szerint „esélye sem volt” Ligetire szavazni, ha akarta volna sem. „De amúgy sem akartam volna, mert bízom a képviselőtársaim értékítéletében” – fogalmazott, hozzátéve, hogy tiszta szívvel szavazott Unger Annára. „Ez nem frakciófegyelem volt, hanem bizalom és összetartás.” Ferenczi Gábor büszke képviselőtársaira, akiken szerinte szintén óriási volt a nyomás. „Lehet itt engem fenyegetni, hogy majd nézzem meg a Medián következő mérését! Van egy rossz hírem! Nem érdekel! Nem közpénzt kilapátolni vagyok itt, nem a karrierért. A rendszerváltásért!” – írta a képviselő. Szerinte ő megcselekedte, amit megkövetelt a haza és egyáltalán nem fog elkeseredni, ha nem lesz már politikus és mehet vissza a családjához. https://www.geosuper.tv/latest/60183-ary.text: Tennis Aryna Sabalenka suffers shock China Open exit Sabalenka faces first Grand Slam-less season since 2022 By Web Desk October 04, 2026 An undated picture of World number two Aryna Sabalenka. — Reuters BEIJING: World number two Aryna Sabalenka suffered a surprise China Open exit after Czech qualifier Nikola Bartunkova produced a major upset to defeat the Belarusian 6-4, 6-3 here at Diamond Court on Saturday. Bartunkova, ranked 34th in the world, continued her breakthrough season by eliminating the second seed in straight sets at the WTA 1000 event. Reflecting on her triumph, Bartunkova said she stayed calm and focused on her own game while expressing her delight at defeating the “legend” Sabalenka. "I focused on myself, to be calm," said Bartunkova, who will face Austria's Sinja Kraus next. "She's a legend, so I'm really happy that I won the match." It is pertinent t to mention that Sabalenka's defeat came a day after top seed Elena Rybakina was also knocked out. The Kazakh, who defeated Sabalenka in last month's US Open final to take over the world number one ranking, lost to Armenian world number 118 Alina Charaeva. It is the first time since 2015 that the top two seeds have failed to reach the China Open round of 16. Sabalenka has endured a difficult season by her high standards and will finish without a Grand Slam title for the first time since 2022. She has also struggled with her emotions on court and has not won a title since completing the Sunshine Double at Indian Wells and Miami in March. Against Bartunkova, she failed to convert any of her five break points and threw her racquet after falling a break behind early in the second set. Europe Chinese State Media Correspondent Goes on Trial in Czech Espionage Case Prosecutors allege that Yang Yiming gathered political and economic intelligence under journalistic cover. His lawyer denies the charges. Save Mark Us Preferred on Google Print The Slezska building of Prague Municipal Court in Prague. The court began hearing the case of Chinese state-media correspondent Yang Yiming, accused of unauthorized activity on behalf of a foreign power, on Oct. 14, 2026. Courtesy of the Ministry of Justice of the Czech Republic Arthur Zhang 10/14/2026 | Updated: 10/15/2026 0:00 X 1 A Chinese state-media correspondent accused of gathering intelligence for Beijing went on trial in Prague on Oct. 14, becoming the first person to be prosecuted under a Czech law targeting unauthorized activities on behalf of a foreign power. Yang Yiming, a Prague correspondent for Guangming Daily, a newspaper operated by the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) Central Committee, denied the charges through his attorney at Prague Municipal Court. Prosecutors allege that Yang used his position as an accredited journalist to collect political and economic intelligence, cultivate influential contacts, and transfer information to China. According to Czech courtroom reporting, state prosecutor Martin Bily said Yang arrived in the Czech Republic in 2022 as a member of a Chinese intelligence service and obtained foreign-journalist accreditation from the Czech Foreign Ministry. The indictment alleges that Yang produced at least 38 documents containing information that he had collected, supplemented by his own assessments, risk evaluations, and recommendations. He allegedly stored the documents electronically and delivered the material to another person at predetermined times and locations. Prosecutors said Yang cultivated relationships with people who could provide useful information, sometimes inviting them to dinners, offering small gifts, or inviting them to conferences in China. Related Stories Thousands of Falun Gong Practitioners March in Prague to Showcase Hope and Resilience ‘Back to the Basics:’ AG Blanche Outlines Top DOJ Priorities The prosecution alleges that his collection and transfer of information threatened the Czech Republic’s sovereignty and constitutional order. Correspondent for CCP-Run Newspaper Yang’s employment at Guangming Daily is documented in the newspaper’s publications. A Jan. 15 article, published shortly before his arrest, identified Yang as its Prague correspondent and carried his analysis of political developments in Poland, the Czech Republic, Hungary, and Slovakia. The report examined the four countries’ relationships with the United States and European Union, their positions on Russia and Ukraine, and economic cooperation with Beijing, including Chinese investments and infrastructure projects in Central Europe. The article documents Yang’s reporting on political and economic affairs but does not establish whether that published work was connected to the activities alleged by Czech prosecutors. Guangming Daily describes itself as a newspaper operated by the CCP Central Committee. Its official institutional history says that since 1994, the newspaper has been an institution directly under the CCP Central Committee and administered by its Central Propaganda Department. First Case Under New Foreign-Power Law Yang was detained in January and subsequently charged with unauthorized activity on behalf of a foreign power. The offense was introduced under Section 318a of the Czech Criminal Code in February 2025. It covers specified activities performed on behalf of a foreign power with the intent to threaten or damage the country’s constitutional order, sovereignty, territorial integrity, defense, or security. A conviction under the provision can carry up to five years in prison. The Czech Constitutional Court upheld the law in February 2026, rejecting a challenge brought by 24 senators. The current Czech government has pledged to repeal the provision, although Justice Minister Jeronym Tejc said in August that he had agreed with judges and prosecutors to refine its wording instead. Defense Disputes Allegations Yang’s attorney, Michal Sykora, rejected the factual allegations, the legal classification of his client’s activities, and the proposed punishment. Sykora argued that prosecutors had failed to identify the specific threat to Czech interests required by law. He said none of the information that Yang allegedly obtained was capable of directly threatening the country’s sovereignty. He maintained that Yang had conducted ordinary journalism and that the case file contained no evidence establishing that he worked for a Chinese intelligence service. Bily disputed those arguments, saying that intelligence collection could be distinguished from legitimate journalism. He said some evidence was classified and could not be publicly disclosed. The court excluded the public during Yang’s questioning and the reading of certain documents, but it rejected the defense’s request to close the entire trial. Bily is seeking an unsuspended prison sentence, a financial penalty, and Yang’s expulsion from the Czech Republic. The hearings are scheduled to continue through Oct. 16.
